name: Big Bend Campground
evidence: --AWH firsthand 'sites adjacent to the water' kept (asked 2026-10-26). Re-audit could not confirm: rec.gov 232019 has no Proximity-to-Water flags; RIVR loop site photos show wooded spurs; FS 'river is located 200 feet from campground'; canopy, RIVR pads ~25-35 m from a side channel, main channel ~60-100 m

name: East Fork Campground
evidence: CampLife site list (2026-10-14 read): RV back-ins 'River Front 2-15' (+12A), all rigs, Water-front amenity; site 4 photo shows open grass to the river. Satellite 38.5440,-79.8250: open grass strip ~40 m from the loop road to the East Fork bank (~25-35 m wide), pads within ~20 m. Pin moved off the rail depot onto the loop

name: Riverside Cabins & RV Park
evidence: satellite 38.9987,-79.0290: riverbank row is cabins/tent ground between the road and the South Branch; RV rows sit ~80-100+ m back behind it, open meadow south. Matches --AWH (RV sites set back); operator 'on the bank' is marketing

name: Riverside Campground
evidence: --AWH firsthand 'several sites back up to the river' kept (asked 2026-10-26). Re-audit: book.wvstateparks.com tags ~24 Riverside sites 'Riverview', none 'Riverfront' (the system uses Riverfront at North Bend); satellite 38.1101,-80.1762 shows the south loop ~35-45 m from the Greenbrier behind a wooded bank strip

name: Summersville Lake Retreat & Lighthouse
evidence: satellite 38.2055,-80.8665 + 0.01 frame: nearest lake arm ~750 m N, ~100 m below (DEM 603->484 m) across continuous forest. Operator FAQ: no direct access; 'stare out on' the lake from premium pull-throughs #1-5/#27-32 is marketing for a distant vista, not a legible overlook

name: Army Camp Rd Campground
evidence: satellite 37.8578,-81.0994 (leaf-off): loop around a clearing ~70-90 m from the New River through continuous woods on all sides; agrees with --AWH (set back in the woods, not waterfront); NPS 'along the banks' is prose

name: Great Bend Campground
evidence: satellite 38.9467,-81.7562 and 38.9462,-81.7578: row of RV pads ~15-30 m from the Sandy Creek backwater (~55-60 m wide, Ohio River pool, so river-sized), open grass under spaced shade trees, picnic tables between pads and bank, boat docks at the west end

name: Stuart Recreation Area
evidence: rec.gov 232007 per-site coords: all 26 sites on the single forested loop (loop roads visible at 38.9183,-79.7765), ~150-200 m from Shavers Fork through woods; the open riverside field with parked vehicles is the day-use/pavilion area (Small Picnic), not campsites. Prior riverview read the day-use field
